newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest hits highs as region's markets stay flat.
newsitem.headline: Budapest hits highs as region's markets stay flat.

text.p: The Hungarian share market tagged on to Wall Street's bull run this week but other east European markets were mostly flat while there was no trading in Bulgaria at all.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) which measures price movements in 50 selected Hungarian, Czech and Polish shares, eased 11.64 points.

Developments in Russia have generally had a strong impact on regional markets but traders said the ouster of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed was unlikely to influence the region's bourses substantially.
BUDAPEST

The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index set new record highs every day this week helped by Wall Street's rise and positive corporate news but by the second half of the week the pace slowed as the market sought new impetus.
"We have reached a level where no major changes can be expected until fresh news comes out," Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities said.
"Two major developments can be expected, one is that Moody's and S&P examine Hungary's rating," he said, adding they might upgrade Hungary's rating to an investment grade.
The other will be a new batch of corporate results, to be released later this month, which traders generally expect to be good.
On Thursday the BUX index closed at 3,728.58 points, up 88.9 points from last Friday.
PRAGUE
Major issues on the Prague bourse rebounded on Thursday but failed to prevent the 13th straight decline on the PX50 index which lost 12.4 points this week to close at 530.0 points.
All the major issues, except savings bank Ceska Sporitelna, recaptured lost ground but traders said there was no evidence that the long awaited upturn on the Prague bourse was about to materialise.

"I don't expect a strong upward movement after today. Supply and demand looks to be in the balance now in the high liquidity shares," said Oldrich Pavlovsky, a trader at Patria Finance investment bank.

Analysts said Czech equities have been hit by a decline in interest from foreign investors who are concerned about the lack of transparency in the capital markets and inadequate protection for minority shareholders' rights.
WARSAW
The WIG index of the Warsaw Stock Exchanges slipped 0.7 percent to 14,821.8 points on Thurdsay and analysts were divided over the market's direction next week, saying the signals were mixed.
Some said the bourse still had growth potential and could find resistance at 15,200 or 15,600 points, especially if companies' September earnings, most of them due on Friday, proved strong.
But others saw the bourse falling to support at 14,400 or even 14,000 points, saying the market's 100-percent rise this year and forthcoming new issues could cool market sentiment.
BRATISLAVA

The Bratislava bourse saw another week of slack trading activity and brokers do not expect the current flat trend to reverse in the near future. The 12-share SAX index advanced 0.69 point to end at 204.51 on Thursday.

"The market would need an increase of trading activity, which would mean the entry of new foreign investors, but the trading is generally expected to remain flat over the next two weeks," said Jozef Cimra of ING Barings.

"Foreign investors seemed to have testing our market over the past few weeks, but an increase in their trading activity would probably require more stable general economic situation in Slovakia," Cimra said.
BULGARIA
No corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week as investors turned towards repo facilities pushing repo turnover to an all-time high.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) closed at 41.28 points, unchanged from last Thursday as there were no deals in corporate papers.
LJUBLJANA

In Ljubljana share prices fell 2.1 percent as the SBI index dropped 27.9 points to 1,271.80. Health resort Terme Catez underperformed the market plummeting 8.9 percent. The biggest gainer, financial consultancy Dadas, soared 11.1 percent.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks traded mixed this week with mild gains in fully listed issues, but traders said they expected an increased market activity and further growth in most stocks in the days ahead.
BUCHAREST

Bucharest prices drifted higher on Thursday after three consecutive sessions of falls. Volumes were modest and traders did not expect turnover to rise substantially before new companies join. The bourse said recently that 14 companies had applied for a listing and would soon be traded.

The VAB-Index, an unofficial value-weighted index of all listed stocks computed by Vanguard SA securities, rose 1.2 percent this week to 295.3 points on Thursday, after touching year lows for the previous three sessions.
TIRANA

The Tirana bourse posted the highest weekly volume of transactions in 364-day T-Bills in its five-month history as 440 million leks worth in T-Bills changed hands during this week's two sessions on Monday and Thursday.
